comment: Shared arrow geometry (tutorial-editor Task 35; F-28). Read by tests/cueGeometry.test.ts now and by screen::render::ass (Task 43, include_str!) later, so the preview's SVG arrow and the rendered ASS arrow are the SAME polygons. Inputs: x,y (tail) and x2,y2 (tip) are normalized fractions of the canvas; stroke is in canvas px. Outputs are canvas px, rounded half away from zero to 2 decimals. Rule: P0=(x*W,y*H), P1=(x2*W,y2*H), d=P1-P0, len=sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) (sqrt, not hypot: IEEE-exact in both languages); len==0 -> expected null. u=d/len, n=(-u.y,u.x). headLength=3*stroke+12, headHalfWidth=2*stroke+5; when len<headLength both scale by len/headLength. B=P1-u*headLength. shaft=[P0+n*s/2, B+n*s/2, B-n*s/2, P0-n*s/2] (s=stroke); head=[P1, B+n*headHalfWidth, B-n*headHalfWidth]. Every expected number below was computed by hand from this rule, not captured from the implementation.

cases.name: diagonal 3-4-5 arrow on the landscape canvas
vertical upward arrow on the portrait canvas
leftward arrow shorter than its head on the 4:3 canvas (head scaled down to the length)
